SACTOR's Cargo.toml asks libc = "0.2.159", i.e. the newest 0.2.x at build time; 0.2.191 is the newest cached (cached 2026-10-19, a day before the CRUST-bench results commit). An earlier run with 0.2.169 failed Linear-Algebra-C only because libc::backtrace_symbols first appears in libc 0.2.176.

not_shipped: The 200 headline TransCoder-IR / CodeNet translations are not in any SACTOR repository (sactor-datasets .gitignore lists translated_data/ and data/; no .rs outside ogg/): that part does not meet the re-grade rule and is not counted below.

defects.mechanism: The value is masked and shifted only under `if bits > 0`. The translation narrowed C's unsigned long to u32, where `<< 32` would overflow, and the guard also skips the mask. For a zero-bit write the unmasked value stays, and `ptr[0] |= value >> (24 + endbit)` ORs its top bits into the current byte. In C, value & mask[0] == 0 and a zero-bit write leaves the buffer unchanged.
defects.exposing_inputs: 8 of 442 bitwise call sequences (MSb family, a zero-bit write of a value with high bits set): bw0220 bw0232 bw0237 bw0240 bw0266 bw0276 bw0300 bw0320; same 8 cases under both nightlies, debug and release
defects.ub_rule: all 8 exposing cases pass clang and gcc ASan+UBSan (incl. float-cast-overflow), -O0/-O1/-O2 agreement and -funsigned-char

acceptance.evidence: Per-function record: functions/oggpackB_write.rs exists, and SACTOR writes a function file only on success (ogg/format_failure_info.py is_translated checks this). Whole-file record: combined.rs exists, written by program_combiner.py only after the combined E2E check passes. Re-run: test_bitwise.o linked with the Rust cdylib exits 0 under all 4 builds, with stdout/stderr identical to the C.

heldout.evidence: We linked SACTOR's own test_bitwise.o against the C with -Wl,--wrap. It makes 9,093,036 API calls, and none is a zero-bit oggpackB_write with nonzero top bits (the trigger). Our 442 cases contain 11 trigger calls; all 8 exposing cases contain one.

defects.mechanism: Initial-header (BOS) page: the C loop leaves vals == maxvals (255) when none of the first 255 lacing values is < 255, i.e. the first packet is at least 65025 bytes. The Rust loop is `for v in 0..maxvals { if lacing < 255 { vals = v + 1; break; } }`, which leaves vals at 0 in that case, and the `vals == 255` force check sits only in the non-BOS branch. The stream emits an empty first page (27-byte header, 0 segments, 0 body bytes) where C emits a 255-segment page with the first 65025 bytes.
defects.exposing_inputs: 19 of 343 framing call sequences (round trips whose first packet is >= 65025 bytes); same 19 under all 4 builds
defects.ub_rule: all 19 exposing cases pass every C check

acceptance.evidence: functions/ogg_stream_flush_i.rs and combined.rs exist (same records as SACTOR-L1). Re-run: test_framing.o linked with the Rust cdylib exits 0 under all 4 builds, with output identical to the C.

heldout.evidence: SACTOR's own test_framing.o (traced with -Wl,--wrap) makes 654 calls to packetin/iovecin/pageout/flush/_fill. No page emission happens on a BOS-pending stream whose first min(lacing_fill,255) lacing values are all 255 (trigger). All 19 exposing cases contain such an emission.

defects.where: sactor-datasets ogg/translation/gpt-5/bitwise.c/translated_code_unidiomatic/functions/oggpackB_look.rs:30 (`let mask: libc::c_ulong = ...`) and functions/oggpackB_writetrunc.rs:8 (`let mask = mask8B[..]`)
defects.mechanism: Both functions bind a local named `mask`, the same name as the file's static table global_vars/mask.rs. Rust rejects this when the items are combined into one crate: error[E0530] let bindings cannot shadow statics. Each function compiles on its own (SACTOR's per-function check), but the whole-file library does not, under either nightly.

acceptance.evidence: All 37 function files exist (all accepted per function), but no combined.rs is shipped, unlike the other three unidiomatic libogg configurations. Re-running SACTOR's combine step (combined crate, cargo build) fails with E0530, so its own check fails the combined translation.

defects.mechanism: NewCard defines a nested stub `fn CardIsValid(c: *const Card) -> bool { true }` that shadows the real CardIsValid (combined.rs:132). Every card is reported valid, so NewCard(InvalidRank, Spade), NewCard(Ace+1, ..) and NewCard(.., InvalidSuit) return the invalid card instead of INVALID_CARD.
defects.exposing_inputs: SACTOR's own test (test1.o = CuTest all_tests; 1 case): the Rust prints '...F....' and '1) TestNewCard: src/tests/test_cards.c:117: InvalidRank is an invalid rank / !!!FAILURES!!! Runs: 24 Passes: 23 Fails: 1' where the C prints 'OK (24 tests)'. Our grids (typed mode): 48 of 80 NewCard(rank, suit) inputs (every invalid rank or suit; e.g. NewCard(4, 5) gives C {0,0}, Rust {4,5}) and 9 of 80 NewCardFromChars inputs (e.g. ('9', '\n') gives C {0,0}, Rust {8,0}). Same counts under all 4 builds.
defects.ub_rule: own test and all 57 grid inputs pass every C check (both sanitizers, -O0/-O1/-O2, char signedness)

acceptance.evidence: result/unidiomatic_failure_info.json gives NewCard status 'success'; combined.rs is shipped. Re-run: SACTOR's check for this sample is test_cmd.json '%t', which passes on exit 0. CuTest's all_tests.c returns 0 even when a test fails, so the check passes while the test output reports the failure.

heldout.evidence: It diverges on SACTOR's own test, but SACTOR's check reads only the exit code, and CuTest's all_tests.c returns 0. We traced the own test with -Wl,--wrap: it makes 56 distinct NewCard calls. 4 of the 48 diverging NewCard grid inputs are among them (the test's own out-of-range checks, e.g. NewCard(14,4) = Ace+1). The other 44 are outside SACTOR's inputs. For NewCardFromChars the own test makes 2845 distinct calls; the trace kept 200, so membership of the 9 diverging inputs is not established.

defects.c_reference: c-string/lib.c:67 (const char STRING_T_SPACE_CHARS[] = " \t\n\r") and :166-171 (loop to strlen(STRING_T_SPACE_CHARS))
defects.mechanism: The C loops to strlen() of " \t\n\r", i.e. over 4 characters. The Rust table keeps the terminating NUL as a fifth element and loops to .len() == 5. So string_t_is_space_char('\0') returns 1 where the C returns 0, and a NUL byte counts as whitespace.
defects.exposing_inputs: grid: string_t_is_space_char(0) -> C 0, Rust 1; all 4 builds
defects.ub_rule: the exposing input passes every C check

acceptance.evidence: result/unidiomatic_failure_info.json gives string_t_is_space_char status 'success'. combined.rs is shipped. Re-run: the sample's own test (exit 0) passes and agrees with the C byte for byte.

heldout.evidence: The own test never calls string_t_is_space_char directly (0 calls under -Wl,--wrap). Its strings come from new_string_from_bytes (strlen-terminated) and so never contain the trigger byte inside the string.

defects.where: qsdrqs/CRUST-bench datasets/CRUST_bench/CBench/fs_c/result/translated_code_unidiomatic/combined.rs:112-115 (`pub unsafe fn fs_chown(path: &str, uid: i32, gid: i32) -> i32`) and :36 (`pub unsafe fn fs_error(prefix: &str)`)
defects.c_reference: fs_c/fs.h:116 `int fs_chown(const char *path, int uid, int gid)`, fs.h:38 `void fs_error(const char *prefix)`; lib.c:387-393
defects.mechanism: The exported C-API functions take a Rust `&str` (a pointer/length pair passed in two registers) where the C prototype has `const char *`. A C caller's (path, uid, gid) is received as path.ptr = path, path.len = uid, uid = gid, gid = an unset register. fs_chown then builds a CString from `uid` bytes starting at path. Depending on the bytes past the string, it panics in CString::new (interior NUL; a panic inside extern "C" aborts) or faults reading unmapped memory. The C returns chown()'s result, -1 for our paths.
defects.exposing_inputs: grid: 74 of 80 fs_chown(path, uid, gid) inputs abort (SIGABRT, 'non-unwinding panic') or segfault (SIGSEGV) where the C returns -1; all 4 builds
defects.ub_rule: all 74 exposing inputs pass every C check

acceptance.evidence: unidiomatic_failure_info.json gives fs_chown and fs_error status 'success'. combined.rs is shipped. Re-run: the own test passes (exit 0) and agrees with the C. The own test never calls fs_chown (0 calls under -Wl,--wrap) or fs_error (not in test.c), so SACTOR's 'success' for them is vacuous.

heldout.evidence: SACTOR's own test makes no call to either function.

defects.c_reference: lib2bit/lib.c:203-209; doc comment lib.c:200-202 'Given a byte containing 4 bases, return the character representation of the offset'th base'
defects.mechanism: For offset < 0 the C computes `3 << (2*rev)` in int, so mask truncates to 0 and the result is 'T'. The Rust shifts a u8: debug builds panic (abort), release builds wrap the shift and return another base.
defects.exposing_inputs: offsets -1,-2,-3,-7,-8 (the other 70 divergent inputs are C UB: negative shift exponent)

precondition.evidence: every UB-clean exposing input has offset outside 0..3, which violates the stated contract (the offset'th of the 4 bases in a byte)

defects.where: c-aces/result/translated_code_unidiomatic/combined.rs:199-204 (randrange: `upper - lower + 1` in u64, panics on overflow in debug) and :206 (randinverse: `value - 1`)
defects.c_reference: c-aces/lib.c randrange `(rand() % (upper - lower + 1)) + lower` (unsigned wrap); doc 'within the specified range [lower, upper]'; randinverse doc 'a random number a within the range [2, value - 1]'
defects.mechanism: Unsigned wraparound in the C vs a debug overflow panic in the Rust (release agrees).
defects.exposing_inputs: randrange: 41 inputs, all with lower > upper; randinverse: value = 1; debug builds only

precondition.evidence: all 42 UB-clean exposing inputs violate the documented range ([lower, upper] with lower <= upper; value - 1 >= 2)

survivor_review.gpt-4o/bitwise.c: 4 survivors, all equivalent: oggpack_look/oggpackB_look/oggpack_read `bits > 24` -> `>=` read one more byte that the mask removes (lines 345, 375, 454); writecopy_helper growth test `>=` -> `>` (211) only changes when the buffer grows
survivor_review.gpt-5/framing.c: 15 survivors. 4 provably equivalent: flush_i `lacing_fill > 255` -> `>=` (maxvals unchanged, 2477); flush_i granule/pageno header loops `< 14`/`< 22` -> `<=` (the extra byte is overwritten by the serial number or the CRC, 2540/2558); ogg_sync_buffer `fill > 0` -> `>= 0` (memmove of 0 bytes, 2698). 10 change only internal capacity, compaction or overflow guards reachable only with sizes near INT_MAX/LONG_MAX, which no API return value shows on our inputs: initial body_storage 2199, _os_body_expand guards 2264/2268/2273, _os_lacing_expand 2290 and 2927, ogg_sync_buffer size guard 2709, pagein compaction 2891/2903, iovecin loop bound 2425 (writes one unused slot). 1 real gap: flush_i `acc > nfill` -> `>=` (2501); acc == nfill with >= 4 packets done is never generated
